findings_unaided: Account 6000 warehouse wages: the table shows a $79,400 variance but S4 says the rise was $74,900, and the two numbers for the same line don't match.
Account 6100 fleet fuel: S9 says it declined $31,600, but the table shows fuel went from $91,200 to $122,800, which is an increase of $31,600, not a decline.
Account 6400 bad debt expense: the table shows a variance of ($52,500) but S3 calls it a reduction of $84,700, so the dollar figure in the text doesn't match the table.

Account 6200 repairs and maintenance: S10 says the depot repair program closed in June with no further spend expected this year, but S11 right after describes $36,400 of July spend as the second phase of that same program.

Account 7400 inventory shrink adjustment jumped $62,300, 700 percent, the biggest percentage move in the whole memo, and it's starred as needing commentary, but none of the sentences mention it at all.

Account 5000 cost of product sold: S5 credits the $147,000 decline to renegotiated inbound freight rates, but the memo says inbound freight is excluded from cost of product sold and sits on its own line, account 5100.

C1.reason: Utilities only moved $3,300 on account 6600, which is well short of the $25,000 leg even with three reasons given, so S7 didn't need to be in the memo at all.

C2.reason: S12 talks about a $12,800 fieldwork invoice landing in August, which is bigger than the $5,300 that actually moved on professional fees, so the timing does look worth questioning.

C3.reason: I don't see a May column anywhere in this memo, it only compares June and July, so I can't check a $214,000 May figure for account 5100 that isn't in the table I read.

C4.reason: This is the same one I flagged, S5 explains the $147,000 cost of product sold move with a freight-rate story, but the memo itself says freight sits outside cost of product sold on its own line.

C5.reason: I already noticed this myself, S4 cites $74,900 for warehouse wages but the table next to account 6000 says the movement was $79,400, so the two figures don't agree.

C6.reason: I took S2 at face value the first time around, but if the $74,400 marketing charge really belongs to a different month than July, then the period in S2 is wrong.

C7.reason: S6 just points to a seasonal slowdown in school nutrition accounts for the $214,000 drop in product revenue, and I don't remember seeing a schedule or account list backing that up.

C8.reason: This is the same gap I flagged, account 7400 shrink moved $62,300 and 700 percent and not one of the twelve sentences mentions it, so it can't go out without a driver.

C9.reason: The table already says software subscriptions moved $1,600 and 5.3 percent for account 6300, not the $16,000 and 53 percent this challenge cites, so the challenge has its own numbers wrong.

C10.reason: I hadn't connected service revenue and depot repairs before, but if $55,000 into account 4100 and $82,200 out of account 6200 are really one transfer, then S1 calling it new contracts isn't the full picture.

C11.reason: S8 already says the June reclassification is complete, but getting the controller to confirm that with the actual closing entry seems like a fair ask on a freight line this small.

C12.reason: This is the one I caught too, S3 calls the bad debt move an $84,700 reduction, but account 6400 in the table only moved $52,500, so the dollar figure in the sentence is wrong.

C13.reason: This is the fuel one I already flagged, account 6100 went from $91,200 to $122,800 in the table, which is a rise, and S9 calls that same movement a decline.

C14.reason: This is the repairs contradiction I already caught, S10 says the program closed in June with nothing more expected, and S11 right after describes $36,400 of active July repair work on the same program.
